judge_notes.opus: E won because it gives each item a reason to care: Carbon priced 'matching its cheaper Argon model rather than a premium tier,' Alibaba 'answered within a day,' and a closing kicker, 'The week's clearest caution came from NEAR AI,' which supplies the significance most rivals lack. F lost on spec stacking and run-ons ('280B-total, 14B-active ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview'; a 60+ word opener joined by 'while'), with B close behind for its ~75-word first sentence fusing Carbon benchmarks with the Anthropic IPO valuation.
judge_notes.glm: F won because it is the only summary with a genuine throughline — competition and timing ('Alibaba answered within a day') plus a real punch in the NEAR AI enclave flaw, and its only caveat ('though it published no model card or benchmarks') is integrated rather than repeated. E is close behind: clean grammar and the $1.4 trillion valuation line gives the IPO real scale, hurt slightly by a benchmark stack and the abrupt license-exclusion ending. K lost because it is the thinnest and vaguest: 'a broader release of its data product' and 'although its license has geographic restrictions' inform the reader of almost nothing, and the IPO — the day's biggest money story — is absent. O and B sit just above K mostly on density: O's 60-word opening sentence ('a day after Anthropic's Fable 5.2 launch ... which TechCrunch says implies') buries three stories in one breath, and B's spec stacks ('280B-total, 14B-active') force rereading.
judge_notes.astra: N wins narrowly because its readable opening culminates in an actual synthesis: "show how labs are packaging AI into customer-facing and productivity workflows." Missing licensing and timing specifics keep it below publication-ready strength. H is the closest challenger, with useful price positioning and a concrete confidentiality failure, but its IPO and robotics detours undermine coherence. G finishes last because its opening runs from "Google made Gemini 4 Carbon broadly available" through "a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.404 trillion" in one heavily loaded sentence, followed by more dense inventories rather than orientation. No entry earns a 4 or 5.
